intent: Put a heading on one of the kit's type ramp roles, with the outline level chosen apart from the look.
typical_uses: The title of a screen or a page section between kit components
A section heading whose outline level differs from its look (an h3 drawn on the heading-1 role)

instead.target: CardTitle, with `render` for the heading element

dont_use_when.situation: The title of an empty state
The title of a page or section header with its actions and meta
Running text, a caption or a meta line

invariants.text: Each typography value sets font size, line height, weight and tracking from the matching `--text-<role>-*` ramp tokens and the family from `--font-heading`; no literal value.
The heading has zero margin on whatever element `render` substitutes; spacing belongs to the layout that places it.
`typography` never changes the element and `render` never changes the class: the outline level and the ramp role are set independently. An explicit `typography={null}` resolves to heading-1.

anti_patterns.dont: Pick the element to get a bigger heading
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pick `typography` for the look and `render` for the outline level

anti_patterns.dont: Add a margin to the heading through className
anti_patterns.do_instead: Space it with the gap of the layout that holds it

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (Heading passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how a caller picks the outline level, such as `render={<h1 />}`.

good.title: A page title on the display role

bad.title: A heading inside a Card
bad.why: The Card's own title part carries the card's title sizing and spacing; use CardTitle with `render={<h3 />}`.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof headingVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The role class-name builder Heading itself uses, exported beside the component.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (Heading passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how a caller picks the outline level, such as `render={<h1 />}`.
